related_questions.question: What is F33.1 major depressive disorder?

text_blocks.snippet: F33.1 is the ICD-10 code for Major Depressive Disorder, Recurrent, Moderate. This means a person experiences recurring episodes of depression, and the current episode is classified as moderate in severity.

list.title: Recurrent:
list.snippet: The individual has had multiple past episodes of major depression.

list.title: Moderate:
list.snippet: The severity of the current depressive episode is considered moderate, falling between mild and severe.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms may include persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities, changes in appetite or sleep, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, difficulty concentrating, and thoughts of death or suicide.

list.title: Impact on daily life:
list.snippet: Moderate depression can significantly impair a person's ability to function in daily life, impacting work, relationships, and overall well-being.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment typically involves a combination of psychotherapy (such as CBT or IPT) and antidepressant medication, along with lifestyle adjustments.
